author: Mark Atwood
text:
Items 12, 13, 14, 15 and 17 fixed. Each was a claim I could check rather than a judgement call; the drifted-duplicate items (7-11) and the baseline re-classification (6) are still open.

14. pkix-chain said Ed25519, P-521 and RSA-PSS were 'tracked under PKIX-gphz'. All three ship: Ed25519Verifier, EcdsaP521Verifier and RsaPssVerifier all exist in pkix-path behind the ed25519/p521/rsa features. Replaced with pkix-path's own canonical sentence so the two cannot drift again.

15. ureq is pinned at 3, which is HTTP/1.1 only, so 'No HTTP/2 connection pooling tuning' named a protocol the dependency does not speak. Now 'No connection-pool tuning'.

17. pkix-profiles' reason for requiring std was false. It said ValidationPolicy 'holds owned Vec fields that currently require the standard allocator' -- but ValidationPolicy is defined in pkix-path, which is no_std + alloc, and Vec is an alloc type. The real reason is std::sync::OnceLock, used by the LintProfile impls to cache their lint lists; OnceLock is in neither core nor alloc. Said so, and dropped the 'planned for a future release' promise: this is a conversion nobody has done, not a blocker.

12. Two findings. The guard in from_pem is no longer a panic workaround -- probed x509-cert 0.3.1 directly: empty input gives Ok(vec![]), whitespace-only and marker-less input give 'PEM error in post-encapsulation boundary', and none of the three panics. So the crate doc was advertising a panic mode that no longer exists; removed. But the guard itself STAYS, for the reason the old comment mentioned almost in passing: it is what makes marker-less input report NoCertificates instead of a PEM error about the shape of the bytes. Added from_pem_degenerate_input_is_no_certificates, which pins both the behaviour and what upstream now does, so the guard's justification is checked rather than cargo-culted.

13. Both trust-store adapters exist, so 'Future' was stale -- but neither depends on pkix-identity, so dropping the word would have made it a false present-tense claim, which is what the bead flagged. Resolved by saying both: the crates ship, neither uses this one, and the bullet is a use the split makes available rather than an attribution.

Version bumps the divergence gate required: pkix-identity 0.3.2, pkix-profiles 0.5.2, pkix-aia-http 0.3.2, pkix-truststore 0.2.2. pkix-chain was already unreleased at 0.9.0.
